title: RL Business Analyst, re:Cycle Reverse Logistics
descriptionHtml:
re:Cycle Reverse Logistics is an electronics processing, reuse, and recycling company that works to extend the life of used electronic equipment through reuse, repair, and recycling. We are a stand-alone company within the Amazon corporate family that provides services to other Amazon companies. We specialize in the handling of valuable electronic equipment that was originally used in data centers. Come join our team and be a part of history as we deliver results for the largest cloud services company on Earth!

re:Cycle Reverse Logistics is looking for a talented, driven, and analytically focused Business Analyst in support of our Reverse Logistics (RL) program. As a Reverse Logistics Business Analyst you will be responsible for developing metrics and dashboards to support multiple initiatives within our global network. Our mission is to manage and scale information technology asset disposition (ITAD) services for used electronics and electronic equipment (UEEE) through secure and environmentally sustainable practices supporting asset recovery, reuse, recycling, and other circular economy initiatives.

In this role, you will be responsible for designing and building the data pipelines, tables, and automated reporting systems that enable our Planning, Operations, and Finance teams to make faster, more accurate decisions. You will develop and maintain data sources that consolidate data from across the RRL network — spanning inbound receipts, facility processing, parts disposition, and outbound logistics — into reliable, queryable data models. You will create and maintain interactive dashboards and self-service analytics tools that track KPIs, support monthly S&OP processes, and provide real-time visibility into capacity, throughput, and operational performance across our global facilities. This role requires deep technical expertise in SQL, data modeling, and pipeline architecture, combined with the ability to understand business context and translate operational needs into scalable data solutions. You will work closely with the reporting and analytics team, planning analysts, operations leaders, and product management to ensure the right data is available at the right time to drive accountability, process improvements, and strategic decision-making.


Key job responsibilities
- Develop and maintain automated reporting solutions and interactive dashboards (QuickSight or similar) that support daily operations, monthly S&OP, capacity planning, and executive-level performance reviews
- Build and optimize data tables and warehouse structures that enable accurate volume projections across the full lifecycle — inbound receipts, facility processing throughput, parts testing and sparing, and outbound disposition
- Partner with planning analysts and product management to translate business requirements into technical data solutions, ensuring tooling and reporting meet evolving operational needs
- Create and maintain data pipelines that feed planning models, forecasting tools, and capacity planning systems used across global facilities
- Develop self-service analytics capabilities that empower operations, planning, and finance teams to independently access and analyze data without ad hoc engineering support
- Establish data quality frameworks, monitoring, and validation processes to ensure accuracy and reliability of reporting across all downstream consumers
- Support cross-functional collaboration by providing analytic roll-ups, data extracts, and custom reporting for Operations, Commercial, Program Management, and Finance leadership
- Document data architecture, pipeline logic, and reporting methodologies to ensure institutional knowledge and enable team scalability
- Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting processes and reduce time-to-insight for key business stakeholders

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Finance, or a related technical field
- 3+ years of business analyst, data analyst or similar role experience
- 3+ years of Tableau Desktop, Quicksight or other relevant data visualization software experience
- 2+ years of SQL experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with data visualization using Tableau, Quicksight, or similar tools
- Experience influencing internal and external stakeholders
- Experience using inventory management systems Warehousing, supply chain, inventory management, finance, vendor and/or project management experience

title: Sr. Tech Program Manager, Data Center Learning
descriptionHtml:
AWS Data Center Learning is hiring a Senior Technical Program Manager to own and sustain the GDCO 7S Continuous Improvement program — the workplace-organization and operational-excellence mechanism that runs across our global data center fleet. The program has moved through its foundation and design phases and is transitioning to a durable, self-sustaining operating model. This role is the owner who takes it to a scaled, mechanism-driven program that runs globally.
You will own the operating and planning mechanisms that keep a large, distributed community of Regional POCs, cluster leaders, and site teams aligned — giving leadership a clear line of sight into audit coverage, compliance, and program health. Day-to-day execution is run by the field; you own the structure they run within: the tooling and data backbone, the standards and communications cadence, and the metrics that measure impact.


Key job responsibilities
Own the program mechanism. Run the 7S operating rhythm end-to-end — monthly audit cycle, findings, implementation plans, metrics, communications, and leadership reviews — as a documented, repeatable mechanism.
Own the tooling & data backbone. Serve as the program owner for the audit platform and the compliance reporting pipeline; ensure audits, scoring, and dashboards operate reliably and that 7S compliance is surfaced in the WBR/leadership dashboards.
Drive standards & single source of truth. Maintain the 7S standards (“What Good Looks Like”), playbooks, and runbooks in Policy 2.0 / Playbook 2.0, and own the 7S wiki as the single source of truth
Measure and prove impact. Define and report the metrics that demonstrate program value and sustainability (audit activity and completion rates, compliance, month-over-month trends) and move the program toward outcome-based measurement.
Scale enablement. Own self-serve enablement — tooling instruction guides and training requirements so new POCs can onboard.
Govern & de-risk. Maintain a light governance and escalation model, manage program risks, reduce duplication with adjacent mechanisms (e.g., GEMBA walks), and keep the program auditable and compliant.
Influence without authority. Earn trust and drive adoption across DCO, Infrastructure Delivery, DCEO, Safety, and Security.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership

title: Area Manager II, YHM2
descriptionHtml:
Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. In this role, you will lead a team of hourly workforce and will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. You will also play a key role in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.

Our fulfillment network launches new Operations sites every year, providing various opportunities for your professional growth. We hire Area Managers based on location preference and the business’ current openings.

Key job responsibilities
- Support, mentor, and motivate your hourly workforce
- Manage safety, quality, productivity, and customer delivery promises
- Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Engineering, Loss Prevention, Quality Assurance, Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies and can be loud
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)

A day in the life
As an Area Manager II at an Amazon fulfillment center, you'll act as a strategic leader overseeing upto 80 associates while driving department level operational improvements. You'll conduct planning sessions with your team, coaching them through operational challenges while developing their leadership capabilities. On a typical day, you'll partner cross-functionally with teams such as Quality, HR, and Safety to implement scalable process improvements that could impact 200+ associates across multiple workflows. You'll diagnose root causes of performance gaps using advanced analytics, facilitate alignment meetings with senior leadership on department-level goals, and make data-driven decisions that balance competing priorities. You would leverage your strategic thinking to review department-wide metrics, and plan initiatives that directly impact millions of customer orders while maintaining high levels of engagement, safety, quality, and productivity standards.

title: Sr Program Manager - Change Management, Hub Delivery
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we are working to be the most Customer-centric company on earth. One customer experience we are constantly looking to take to the next level is how we fulfill and deliver orders. We are doing so by building a world-class last mile operation that exceeds the expectations of our customers by ensuring their orders are delivered quickly, accurately, and cost-effectively.

Amazon Hub Delivery enables local small businesses to partner with Amazon and provide flexible, cost-effective delivery service that delights customers globally. As an emerging Amazon Logistics delivery channel, Hub Delivery is on an exponential growth trajectory worldwide.

Hub Delivery is looking for a Change Management Sr. Program Manager to run the day-to-day governance operation through which all operational, technology, and policy changes impacting Hub Delivery partners and delivery associates are assessed, approved, and deployed across 7+ countries. You will be the operator of the framework: processing intakes, assessing impact and risk, sizing complexity, routing stakeholder approvals through senior leadership gates, enforcing freeze calendars across global peak events, managing readiness periods, and handling exception escalations. This is a hands-on execution role. You are the person cross-functional teams come to when they need to launch a change and need to know what approvals are required, what the timeline looks like, and whether the freeze window allows it. You will partner with cross-functional leaders across operations, product, network planning, quality, finance, risk, and regional teams to ensure changes are visible, sequenced, and governed consistently worldwide. This role also requires strong collaboration with Communications, Learning & Development, and worldwide delivery program Change Management teams to align processes and enablement programming across delivery channels.

Key job responsibilities
- Process and manage all change management intakes end-to-end: assess scope and risk, size complexity, prioritize, and route through the appropriate governance and approval path
- Enforce freeze calendars and readiness periods across global peak events, managing restricted and blocked windows for 7+ countries
- Route stakeholder approvals through senior leadership gates, track alignment, and escalate when timelines are at risk
- Manage exception requests during freeze periods, ensuring proper justification and leadership sign-off before any change proceeds
- Partner with Communications and Learning & Development teams to coordinate partner-facing messaging, training, and enablement for each change
- Collaborate with worldwide delivery program Change Management teams to align frameworks and drive process consistency across delivery channels
- Identify patterns across intakes to codify repeatable components, close parity gaps between regions, and eliminate scale blockers
- Develop metrics and post-launch review processes to measure change effectiveness, track adoption, and surface improvement opportunities
- Operate autonomously with minimal oversight, managing a high volume of concurrent changes across multiple regions and stakeholder groups

About the team
The Hub Delivery program is part of Amazon's fast growing last mile delivery program worldwide. We partner with customer obsessed small business owners who then deliver to Amazon customers. Our partners raise the bar for the delivery experience, in some of the most complex last mile scenarios!

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

title: Business Coach, Amazon, VAS-Category
descriptionHtml:
Equal parts advisor and operating partner, Amazon’s team of Business Coaches assist and guide our Delivery Service Partner (DSP) business owners as they build and grow successful last mile package delivery businesses during a transformational time.

The Business Coach finds and executes value-creation opportunities and manages the DSP relationship across the entire lifecycle of the business. As trusted advisors, Business Coaches work alongside DSPs to help solve their biggest challenges at a programmatic level; influence their business planning and strategy; and look around corners to identify obstacles and recommend solutions, ensuring DSP owners make effective business decisions and are setup for success.

Our Business Coaches are leaders and collaborators. They are analytical and creative; deadline-driven, organized and able to multi-task; and have strong interpersonal skills including a demonstrated ability to earn trust, inspire others, and be empathetic. You’ll be at the center of cross-functional teams, all working together to deliver the highest quality experience to Amazon customers.

If you're a dynamic, organized self-starter who’s ready to partner with our DSP owners as they launch and scale their business in one of the fastest growing industries in the world, we’d like to talk with you. Curious? Good, that’s one of our Leadership Principles! Discover more about the opportunity below.

Key job responsibilities
On a daily basis, Business Coaches are responsible for:

Supporting owners as they onboard to the program and prepare to launch.
Guiding owners as they scale their business and manage operational issues, ensuring they have resources in place to effectively ramp-up operations and prepare for peak periods.
Coordinating Business and Financial Health Reviews to discuss business performance and new opportunities, as well as to provide benchmarking data and insights.
Identifying workflow inefficiencies and working to formulate and implement operational improvements at the network level and to improve the individual DSP owner experience.

A day in the life
As a Business Coach, you will partner with 20-40 DSP owners assigned to delivery stations across IN. You’ll work closely with a portfolio of owners at different stages as they set strategy, help drive accountability and engagement, and motivate and track key performance metrics. You’ll collaborate with an integrated internal team of Station Operations Managers, Program Managers, and Compliance and Finance personnel to ensure owners launch and scale their business in compliance with program requirements. Together, you’ll provide best-in-class support for owners by removing obstacles and improving financial, operational, and safety practices at the network level. You’ll accomplish this by analyzing problems, discovering insights, delivering recommendations, and driving change both internally and externally.

title: Associate Solutions Architect Internship 2027
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon Web Services (AWS) as an Associate Solutions Architect Intern and launch your career in cloud computing. Available to work full-time for either 3 or 6 months during 2027, you'll gain hands-on experience designing cloud and generative AI solutions, learning from experienced architects, and working on real AWS projects that impact millions of customers worldwide.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's leading cloud computing platform, helping millions of customers — from startups to global enterprises — build and run applications without managing physical servers. We're seeking motivated individuals for our Associate Solutions Architect Intern program, a structured learning experience designed to develop the next generation of Cloud Solutions Architects.

This internship serves as a pathway to our Solutions Architect Graduate Program, offering you the opportunity to build foundational knowledge in cloud computing, AWS services, and solutions architecture principles in a supportive, education-first environment. You'll learn to understand customer requirements, build working cloud and AI solutions, and communicate technical recommendations effectively while being mentored by experienced Solutions Architects.

Key job responsibilities
Complete a structured training curriculum to build cloud architecture foundations and develop expertise in AWS services
Analyze customer requirements and learn to translate them into technical solution recommendations
Participate in solution design sessions and observe customer engagements with experienced Solutions Architects
Work on a real AWS project, applying architecture principles and building hands-on experience with AWS services
Develop communication skills by learning to present technical concepts effectively to diverse audiences

A day in the life
As an Associate Solutions Architect Intern, you'll engage in a mix of structured learning and practical application. Your day might include attending training sessions on AWS services and the Well-Architected Framework, then applying those concepts to a real project you're building on AWS. You'll participate in solution design discussions, observing how experienced architects translate customer needs into technical recommendations. You might shadow customer engagements to see how solutions are presented to diverse audiences, then return to work on your own project, experimenting with AWS services and architecture principles. Throughout your internship, you'll develop presentation skills by communicating technical concepts to colleagues and mentors, receiving feedback that helps you grow as a solutions architect.

About the team
We are the EMEA Student Programs Team within AWS, dedicated to nurturing emerging talent in cloud computing. Our team collaborates across the organization to create meaningful internship experiences that bridge the gap between academic learning and real-world cloud architecture. We work with experienced Solutions Architects who are committed to mentoring the next generation of cloud professionals. Together, we're building a community of architects who understand how to solve complex business problems through innovative cloud solutions. When you join us, you'll be part of a team that values your growth, supports your learning journey, and helps you develop the skills needed to succeed in cloud consulting and solutions architecture.

Basic qualifications

- Currently enrolled in penultimate or final year of a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical field, graduating in 2027 or 2028

- Experience with at least one modern programming language (such as Python, Java, C++, or JavaScript)

title: Senior Reliability Maintenance Engineering Technician, RME
descriptionHtml:
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team is central to Amazon's commitment to innovation. As Amazon evolves and adapts, this team makes sure that the tools and technologies we use do as well. As a Senior RME Technician, you'll help us stay one step ahead, adopting the latest technologies and identifying new and efficient ways of working. In this role, you’ll pay close attention to our processes to help maintain our high standards, and you’ll put in place upgrades to take that standard even higher.

Key job responsibilities
Demonstrate best practice on using equipment safely and monitor teams to ensure everyone follows the correct processes
Keep track of equipment performance through visual checks, condition-based monitoring, and preventative maintenance tasks and schedule additional servicing when required
Supervise technicians on shift to support their development and act as the first point of contact for Reliability Maintenance Engineers
Solve issues in equipment to reduce downtime for operations so they can process packages as quickly as possible
Support in finding ways to continually improve systems and standardise processes across the EU network

A day in the life
In every shift, you’ll be leading a team to make sure everyone has the equipment they need and that it’s running properly. That involves monitoring processes so that regulations and policies are followed and ensuring that preventative maintenance is carried out to increase equipment uptime.

With everything you observe on your shifts, you’ll suggest improvements to make our systems more efficient and productive and then implement those improvements across an EU-wide function. You’ll also be monitoring processes with tools like Scada to guarantee their performance, as well as working closely with your line manager to assist with admin tasks.

This role is located at one of our operational sites. You’ll work shift patterns, which may include some weekends and nights. As you develop your experience within this exciting part of Amazon, you’ll be well-placed to progress into more senior roles.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or cutting-edge tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

Basic qualifications

- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year UK certified apprenticeship
- Experience working as a technical lead
- Experience in electrical or mechanical engineering
- Experience in material handling equipment (MHE) or automation environments, or experience in similar environments
- Experience leading engineering teams as a mentor or tech lead, or experience leading and influencing your team or organization
- Advanced proficiency in verbal and written English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in a multi-site environment
- Experience in PLC based controls design, development, implementation and support
- Experience working with CMMS software, or experience in planning, scheduling and auditing maintenance activities
- Bachelor's degree or above in Engineering (any domain), Operations, Business Administration, or a related field

title: Software Development Engineer, Lambda Runtimes, AWS
descriptionHtml:
AWS Lambda’s goal is nothing less than to simplify and improve the experience of computing in the cloud for every developer on the planet, from start-ups to the largest Fortune 100 companies. Serverless computing is rapidly changing how every company thinks about building and delivering software solutions, and Lambda is leading this industry wide effort.

Our Team

AWS Lambda is growing its initiatives in Dublin, Ireland, with goals of continuing to define the Serverless revolution. Lambda teams in Dublin are part of lambda experience charter with mission to simplify the developer, operator, and administrator tasks in bringing code from desktop-development to a production service. If you’re excited by Serverless computing, programming languages and container/function interaction models, this role is for you. Join us and change how the world computes by enabling new frameworks that enable customers to build better software on top of AWS.

Lambda Experience Runtimes is one of the most customer visible and developer commented upon areas of Lambda. The Language Runtimes team are responsible for the curation, patching and deprecation of all the six Managed Runtimes that Lambda supports such as Python, NodeJS, Java, Ruby, Go, DotNet in addition to the custom runtime plus the associated lambda container images.

An ideal candidate has experience delivering new initiatives and be comfortable working closely with Customers. You should be aware of industry best practices & patterns in all aspects of building, releasing & verifying software. You should also be familiar with industry trends in programming languages, build tooling, and deployment spaces. You will own and help driving exciting new and existing initiatives in Lambda, while being capable of working on massive scale, high availability, and ambiguous performance problems as well as developer experience problems. This role will involve identifying and solving problems in different programming language ecosystems, enabling new customer facing functionality, and new programming paradigms in the Serverless ecosystem.

What does it take to succeed in this role?

A roll-up-your-sleeves type. Comfortable working in an environment dedicated to meeting the expectations and requirements of customers. Able to think about business opportunities, operational issues, and architectural diagrams in the course of a single conversation. Intellectually curious, always looking to learn, and a dedication to turning developers into fans. Someone who makes the team both productive and a fun place to work. Being excited to learn from others while bringing your own novel capabilities and perspectives.

On-Call Responsibility

This position involves on-call responsibilities, every builder on Lambda is also an owner. Nobody likes to get paged in the middle of the night or on the weekend, so we work to ensure that our systems are well engineered, fault tolerant and meet a high quality bar before the go into production. Our customers expect nothing less. When we do get paged we work together as a team to resolve the root cause of the issue and nobody is left on their own to deal with an operational issue.

What you should expect?

If you’re excited by defining how modern and future software applications are built and want to help lead from the innovative edge, we guarantee that your work in our team will be ground-breaking and challenging. We’re looking for a new teammate who is enthusiastic, empathetic, curious, motivated, reliable, and able to work effectively with a diverse team of peers; someone who will help us amplify the positive & inclusive team culture we’ve been building.

Together, we’ll deliver the next generation of industry-leading compute features and help every business from the smallest startups to the largest enterprises run their code in the cloud without the burden of infrastructure or scale (that’s our job). We’ll shape not just our own products, but contribute to the direction of AWS and the serverless industry.

Utility Computing (UC)
AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations — from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS’s services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you’ll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (Iot), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS. Within AWS UC, Amazon Dedicated Cloud (ADC) roles engage with AWS customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services.



Come help us change the world!

Job location is Dublin, Ireland. Relocation assistance available. For more information on Amazon Web Services, please visit http://aws.amazon.com


About the team
About AWS

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

title: Talent Marketing Manager, AIM (Attraction, Influence and Marketing)
descriptionHtml:
We're reinventing how to attract and hire quality talent at scale — come join us.

We're seeking a Talent Marketing Manager to lead the strategy, execution and performance behind two of the AIM organization's most critical marketing functions: activation management and integrated marketing and campaign planning across Workforce Staffing's global hiring portfolio. This role starts with the customer: understanding hiring needs, translating them into marketing goals, and owning how those goals are achieved. You define how marketing support is prioritized, how campaigns are strategically planned, measured and optimized, and how the team scales its impact through automation, data-driven decisioning, and cross-functional orchestration.

You help thousands of people get a job every year.

As a marketing strategist and cross-functional operator, you set the vision for how activation logic, campaign planning, override management, and performance optimization work together to drive fill rate outcomes at scale across priority geographies globally. You translate complex performance data into decisive activation recommendations, manage daily pacing and spend governance, and own the narrative for senior leadership. You flex between deep-focus, data-rich environments and wide-focus, relationship-heavy environments with equal confidence.

You shape organizational strategy, build trust, drive clarity, and solve problems before they escalate.

Your insights don't just inform decisions — they define them. You influence partner team roadmaps and align business managers on fill risk strategy, and represent both the activation and campaign functions in cross-functional planning. You identify gaps between teams and processes, hold partner teams accountable for improvements, and build scalable mechanisms that outlast your direct involvement. You build the trust, mechanisms, and reporting that close the existing gap. You don't wait for perfect data — you make decisions with what exists and build toward what's needed.


Key job responsibilities
Performance Optimization & Marketing Strategy: Define the annual marketing strategy and plan the direction for channel mix, spend efficiency, fill rate improvement, and labor order trajectory across your portfolio. Lead quarterly strategy reviews, updating priorities based on performance data, market shifts, and evolving business needs. Partner with analytics teams to move beyond single-metric measurement to comprehensive campaign performance frameworks. Push back on media recommendations with data where channel performance does not support continued investment.

Activation Strategy & Risk Management: Own the strategic framework for weekly marketing activation logic across assigned markets, including application need and paid application need assessments. Define the override governance model, ensuring decisions are logged and structured to accelerate automation development. Set the standard for how risk is identified, escalated, and resolved across the portfolio.

Integrated Campaign Planning & Execution: Own annual integrated campaign plans for assigned markets, with focus on building and testing during low-volume periods and maintaining readiness for high-volume hiring events. Lead working-backwards planning from hiring projections, site capacity, and historical performance data. Consult senior leadership on quarterly strategy, budget allocation, and major campaign pivots. Translate changing labor order visibility into dynamic marketing adjustments, flagging risks and mitigation plans early.

Cross-Functional Orchestration: Drive collaboration with Performance Marketing, Journey Orchestration, Creative, Talent Engagement, Marketing Analytics, and Business stakeholders. Manage stakeholder expectations across business partners, country leads, and global teams. Bridge the gap between marketing capabilities and operational hiring realities. Manage a wide portfolio of countries with varying levels of data maturity, labour order certainty, and stakeholder sophistication.

Pacing & Spend Governance: Oversee daily pacing reviews, implementing ramp-down or pause decisions when application delivery targets are met. Share insights with Performance Marketing to improve paid marketing efficiency. Own escalation thresholds and spend decision governance.

Stakeholder Communication & Alignment: Own weekly and monthly Business Review deep dive presentations for senior leadership, translating risk sites and marketing performance into clear strategic narrative. Maintain regular alignment with Business Managers and cross-functional partners on fill rate risk and marketing actions. Influence investment priorities and partner team roadmaps through data-driven business cases. Adapt communication to audience maturity — from sophisticated data-driven forums to foundational trust-building conversations.

Application Quality & Fill Rate Improvement: Monitor performance against goals including fill rate, non-paid application share, spend per hire, and application-to-usable application ratios. Implement data-driven optimisations for underperforming sites. Identify quality gaps (geo-targeting, shift messaging, channel mix) and coordinate with Paid Marketing, Creative, and Owned Marketing teams to resolve. Own the activation logic that balances cost efficiency with fill rate delivery.

Automation & Process Improvement: Identify, develop, and drive adoption of mechanisms that improve activation efficiency, reduce manual override volume, and accelerate the path to automated decisioning. Own the automation of campaign planning processes — from discovery through recommendation to implementation. Eliminate redundant workflows and hold partner teams accountable for process improvements across both functions.


A day in the life
Your morning starts with reviewing overnight pacing data across your markets and making activation decisions for the day. You join the weekly reporting call with your stakeholders, leading the marketing view for your area with a clear recommendation for each at-risk site. Mid-morning, you're on a stakeholder call with business partners in Brazil translating application pacing risk into language they understand and building alignment on marketing levers available. After lunch, you're deep-diving a high-spend site in Germany where channel efficiency has dropped — pulling site-level data, identifying the issue, and producing an internal discussion analysis for the Paid Marketing team. In the afternoon, you're working through quarterly initiatives with other teams — defining what to learn, which markets to test in, and how results will inform next quarter's strategy. Later, you prepare the MBR narrative for senior leadership, connecting this month’s activation decisions to fill rate outcomes. You close the day connecting the dots: what patterns are emerging across your portfolio, what's working, what needs to change, and how to translate that into the quarterly strategy update you're presenting to leadership next week.

About the team
Workforce Staffing (WFS) hires thousands of Amazonians every year. The Attraction, Influence, and Marketing (AIM) team achieves high-volume hiring goals by delivering exceptional, multi-channel candidate experiences — engaging and hiring job seekers with maximum efficiency and precision. Leveraging paid digital advertising, owned channels, web experience, and local grassroots efforts, AIM delivers quality candidates at scale. Practicing transformational thinking empowered by leading-edge tech and tool development, this team constantly innovates new processes to increase marketing efficacy.

Basic qualifications

- Experience using data and metrics to measure impact and determine improvements
- Experience in marketing or marketing research
- Experience presenting metrics and progress to goal to senior leadership
- Experience driving direction and alignment with cross-functional teams
- Experience with Excel or Tableau (data manipulation, macros, charts and pivot tables)

Preferred qualifications

- Experience using SQL to pull data and metrics to deliver reports

title: Senior HW Material Engineer, Nitro Team, Annapurna Labs
descriptionHtml:
Annapurna Labs is the team behind the custom silicon and systems at the heart of AWS (Amazon Web Services) infrastructure — we operate like a start-up with the scale of the world's largest cloud provider.

The Nitro HW team at Annapurna Labs is looking for an experienced and technically deep Senior Material Engineer. In this role, you will be the primary technical owner for materials engineering across all Nitro card development — spanning PCB material selection and characterization, hybrid stackup design, and mechanical/thermal materials for the full Nitro portfolio. You will work cross-functionally with HW design, signal and power integrity, mechanical engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain teams to drive material decisions that balance performance, reliability, and long-term supply security.

As a senior engineer, this role goes beyond executing standard material engineering tasks. You are expected to challenge conventions, push the boundaries of what is achievable through rigorous experimentation, and introduce new materials and methodologies that enable next-generation Nitro cards hardware. You will lead complex material-related debug investigations during the cards development, define test and characterization methodologies, and represent Annapurna Labs with third-party vendors and suppliers as the technical authority for materials during card development and NPI.

Key job responsibilities
PCB Domain

title: Reliability Maintenance Engineering Technician, STN8 RME
descriptionHtml:
The Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team at Amazon is fundamental to our operations – they’re the ones keeping vital machinery running at all times. As an RME Technician, you’ll maintain a wide range of equipment and workspaces while upholding Health and Safety best practices. You'll help to keep your colleagues safe and prevent machine downtime. Our RME Technicians boost the availability and quality of our equipment and work to enhance the operational environment too.

Key job responsibilities
Proactive and preventative maintenance tasks on a wide range of site equipment
Carry out reactive repairs and fault diagnosis in a live distribution warehouse
Use the latest tools to maximise equipment effectiveness
Uphold all health and safety policies and practices
Support the development and progression of on-site apprentices
Work on continuous improvement projects and roll out best practices across a range of EU sites

A day in the life
Our RME Technicians are based on-site, so they can respond quickly to any machinery issues. You’ll carry out a range of planned preventative maintenance to our sites’ equipment to make sure it’s working safely. As an RME Technician, you’ll also respond promptly to breakdowns, investigating, finding, and implementing solutions as quickly as possible. You’ll also make suggestions for long-term improvements.

Working alongside senior colleagues, you’ll undertake day-to-day maintenance tasks and will liaise with contractors if you need external expertise. You’ll work on a range of shifts to make sure our sites are supported around the clock – allowing Amazon to deliver at the speed we’re known for.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or innovative tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year UK certified apprenticeship
- Experience in electrical or mechanical engineering
- Experience in electrical or mechanical engineering, or experience in facilities management
- Experience in engineering
- Advanced proficiency in the local language verbally and in writing

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with predictive and preventative maintenance, repair, troubleshooting, and diagnostics on material handling equipment (MHE) and automated conveyor systems
- Experience with deployment and usage of monitoring systems
- Experience working with print and apply machines

This position within the AWS AI team presents a unique and rare opportunity to get in on the ground floor within a fast growing business and help shape the technology, product and the business. A successful candidate will bring deep technical and software expertise, desire to have an industry wide impact and ability to work within a fast moving, startup environment in a large company to rapidly deliver services that have a broad business impact.

Key job responsibilities
• Design and implement core runtime infrastructure components including control plane APIs, data plane execution environments, and deployment orchestration systems
• Build managed runtime capabilities that eliminate Docker complexity and enable rapid iteration for developers (ZIP-based deployments, dependency management, cold
start optimization)
• Optimize agent invocation latency, cold start performance, and resource utilization across Lambda Sandbox, Snapstart, and custom compute platforms
• Develop monitoring, observability, and operational tooling to ensure production reliability and enable rapid incident response
• Collaborate with AWS Lambda, Bedrock, and open-source framework teams (LangChain, LangGraph, Strands) to integrate and optimize agent runtime capabilities
• Contribute to technical strategy and architecture decisions for session management, identity/permissions, cross-account access, and security integrations

title: Software Development Engineer, WW Returns and Recommerce
descriptionHtml:
Not many teams aspire to zero. Welcome to the Worldwide Returns and ReCommerce team (WWR&R) at Amazon.com.

WW R&R is an agile, innovative organization dedicated to ‘making zero happen’ to benefit our customers, our company, and the environment. The mission of WWR&R is to eliminate defects that cause returns (Zero defects), deliver Zero cost of returns for Amazon and send Zero product waste to landfill “the 3 Zeros”. We do this by developing products and driving unparalleled operational excellence to help customers keep what they buy, recover returned & damaged product value, and create the best customer returns experience in the world.
Amazon WW R&R is comprised of business, product, operational, program, software engineering and data teams that manage the life of a returned or damaged product from a customer to the warehouse and on to its next best use. Our work is broad and deep: we train machine learning models to automate routing and find signals to optimize re-use; we invent new channels to give products a second life; we develop world-class product support to help customers love what they buy; we pilot smarter product evaluations; we work from the customer backward to find ways to make the return experience remarkably delightful and easy; and we do it all while scrutinizing our business with laser focus.

As a member of this team, your mission will be to design, develop, document and support massively scalable, distributed real time systems. Using C++, Java, object oriented design patterns, distributed databases and other innovative storage techniques, you will build and deliver software systems that support complex and rapidly evolving business requirements.

We are looking for software engineers with 4+ years of solid Software engineering experience involving solving complex problems. They will get to work on some of the key initiatives planned to support our rapid evolution and growth and in the process solve some of the most challenging problems. These engineers will provide the technical leadership to the team, drive best practices, mentor other engineers and drive continuous improvements in engineering excellence.
We are a group that has fun at work while driving incredible customer, business, and environmental impact. We are backed by a strong leadership group dedicated to operational excellence that empowers a reasonable work-life balance. As an established, experienced team, we offer the scope and support needed for substantial career growth.

Amazon is earth’s most customer-centric company and through WW R&R, the earth is our customer too. Come join us and innovate with the Amazon Worldwide Returns & ReCommerce team!

You'll work in state-of-the-art laboratories, operating advanced testing equipment, executing experiments, and generating critical data that enables our team to make informed decisions about materials that touch millions of customer experiences daily.

Key job responsibilities
Materials Testing & Characterization:
- Conduct hands-on materials testing using equipment including tensile testers, burst testers, tear testers, rheometers, and other materials characterization tools.
- Execute test protocols following TAPPI, ASTM, ISO, and ISTA standards as well as internal developed methods.
- Perform testing on packaging materials including paper substrates, adhesives, coatings, and alternative fiber materials.
- Operate and maintain laboratory equipment, ensuring proper calibration and functionality
- Prepare test and store specimens according to specifications and standard operating procedures
- Identify, recommend, and help implement improved lab processes for the team. Learning to create mechanisms.

Data Collection & Analysis:
- Collect, organize, and document experimental data with high accuracy and attention to detail.
- Analyze test results and identify trends or anomalies in materials performance.
- Generate clear and concise test reports summarizing findings and observations.
- Support data-driven decision making by providing reliable, high-quality test results

Laboratory Operations:
- Follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work instructions for all testing activities
- Maintain a safe, clean, and organized laboratory environment.
- Participate in laboratory safety programs and equipment maintenance schedules.
- Assist in identifying opportunities to improve testing efficiency and data quality.
- Support inventory management of laboratory supplies and test materials

Cross-Functional Support:
- Collaborate with Advanced Materials Engineers and scientists on experimental design and execution.
- Communicate test results, status updates, and any issues or blockers to team members.
- Support supplier qualification activities by conducting materials testing on vendor samples.
- Assist with sample preparation and testing for field trials and deployment validation.
- Participate in team meetings and contribute to project planning discussions.

Documentation & Continuous Improvement:
- Contribute to the development and refinement of test procedures and SOPs
- Document experimental procedures, observations, and results clearly and thoroughly.
- Identify and recommend improvements to testing methods and laboratory processes.
- Learn and apply materials science principles to understand the significance of test results.
- Seek feedback and continuously develop technical skills and domain knowledge.

Work Environment:
- Primarily laboratory-based work with hands-on equipment operation.
- Standard lab safety protocols and PPE requirements.
- Occasional lifting of materials and equipment (up to 50 lbs), standing, walking, kneeling throughout the day.
- Collaborative team environment with regular interaction with scientists and engineers.

A day in the life
Your day starts in the lab preparing test specimens—cutting paper samples to precise dimensions and conditioning them in the environmental chamber. You're supporting a critical adhesive development project, and today's testing will determine if the new formulation meets performance requirements.

Mid-morning, you're running tensile and burst tests on paper samples, carefully following the test protocol and recording data in real-time. The results look interesting—you notice the tear strength is higher than previous samples and flag this for the materials engineer leading the project.

After lunch, you're operating the rheometer to characterize viscosity profiles of new hot melt adhesive samples from three different suppliers. You meticulously document the temperature ramps and flow behavior, knowing this data will directly inform sourcing decisions.

Your afternoon includes calibrating equipment, organizing test data into clear summary reports, and preparing samples for tomorrow's environmental conditioning tests. You also participate in a team meeting where you present your week's testing results—your data shows one supplier's material consistently outperforms the others.
This is hands-on work that matters. The tests you conduct today generate the data that enables breakthrough materials innovations, supports major procurement decisions, and ultimately improves packaging for millions of customers while advancing Amazon's sustainability goals.

Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:

1. Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
2. Maternity and Parental Leave Options
3. Paid Time Off (PTO)
4. 401(k) Plan

If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

About the team
The Global Materials Science (GMS) organization is Amazon's Center of Excellence for packaging materials development and supply chain transformation. Our team represents a fundamental shift in how Amazon approaches packaging innovation—owning the invention, development, and optimization of materials that power our fulfillment network.

Our Mission: We build deep expertise in packaging materials through rigorous research and testing, develop innovative packaging solutions that unlock automation potential and sustainability improvements, and establish robust supply chains that deliver superior solutions at lower cost.

Our Vision: To be the global leader in e-commerce packaging materials science and innovation, enabling the best customer packaging experience at the lowest cost to serve.

What Makes Us Unique: We're not just specifying materials—we're fundamentally understanding them through the materials science triangle framework (processing, structure, properties). Our integrated capabilities span from molecular-level materials characterization, to full packaging system testing, to automation compatibility testing. This end-to-end ownership enables us to innovate faster, unlock step-change improvements previously thought impossible.

Our Impact: We're driving Amazon's transition from plastic to paper packaging, developing breakthrough materials and establishing supply chains that reduce costs while advancing our 2040 net-zero commitment. Our work directly influences automation success, customer experience, and sustainability metrics.

Our Culture: We operate with high technical rigor while moving at startup speed. We embrace calculated risk-taking in R&D, fail fast, and iterate based on data. We believe in radical collaboration—our success requires seamless partnership across engineering, procurement, operations, and sustainability teams. We value both technical excellence and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Our Team: We bring together materials scientists, chemists, engineers, lab technicians, and program managers who are passionate about solving hard problems. We partner with world-class academic institutions, leading materials suppliers, and internal Amazon teams to push the boundaries of what's possible in packaging materials.

And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Infrastructure Operations (Data Center) team is the backbone of AWS, supporting the rapidly growing AWS business and customers 24/7. We are looking for a Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) Engineer with experience in critical facilities management, a result-driven individual with strong technical (electrical/mechanical) understanding and the drive and vision to take our data center engineering operations to the next level. The role will report to the DCEO Manager and be responsible for sustaining availability, cost management, risk assessment and mitigation, review corrective and preventative maintenance of critical infrastructure and metric reporting.

title: Principal CSM-T, EC2 Capacity
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform, and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) is its largest and most consequential service. As customers accelerate workloads spanning generative AI training and inference, large-scale analytics, and mission-critical production systems, AWS’s ability to plan, commit, and deliver compute capacity at scale is a defining competitive advantage. As an AWS Principal Customer Solutions Manager-Tech (Principal CSM-T) in the EC2 Capacity Customer Experience organization, you will lead the most strategic capacity engagements for AWS’s largest global compute and ML customers, owning the strategic planning of their long-range capacity solutions and creating sustained business value through the reliable delivery of compute at scale.

You identify and solve the most intrinsically complex business and technical problems in capacity across multiple business units, geographies, and customers, with solutions that are as simple as possible. You lead and execute engagements in highly undefined and rapidly evolving environments, creating and shaping long-range capacity strategies where information is incomplete or conflicting, and creating structure and clarity for customers, partners, executives, and internal teams. Using exceptional judgment and deep technical acumen, you drive these initiatives from ambiguity to measurable results and value realization. You bring focus and strategic direction across enterprise-wide capacity initiatives and cross-organizational teams, aligning entire organizations around shared outcomes measured in billions of dollars of customer workload.

You orchestrate execution across enterprise workload portfolios by aligning business and technical priorities with internal and external stakeholders, ensuring long-term value realization. You translate significantly complex technical and supply concepts into clear recommendations and strategies that change how organizations plan and commit capacity at scale. You apply advanced technical expertise and rapidly adopt emerging technologies, including AI, to navigate complexity and make the critical decisions that keep multi-quarter and multi-year capacity plans on track. You earn customer trust as a strategic advisor through solving their most complex capacity challenges, and you demonstrate exceptional communication skills across all organizational levels, up to and including the C-suite, independently presenting to executive audiences. Every initiative you deliver is measured not only by its immediate success but by the mechanisms and best practices it leaves behind, raising the bar for what AWS and customers can jointly achieve.



Key job responsibilities
As a Principal Capacity CSM-T, you will:
• Lead the most strategic, enterprise-wide capacity engagements for AWS’s largest global compute and ML customers, identifying and solving highly complex business and technical problems across multiple business units, geographies, and partner organizations.
• Own and drive long-range (multi-quarter and multi-year) capacity and scaling plans that translate customer growth forecasts into concrete infrastructure commitments, and own the end-to-end accountability for delivering against them.
• Serve as a trusted advisor to senior executive stakeholders, up to and including the C-suite, shaping long-term capacity, cloud, and AI strategy and influencing critical capital-allocation decisions.
• Organize complex demand signals into supportability scenarios that enable VP+ leaders to make informed capital allocation decisions, partnering with Supply Chain and Finance to quantify trade-offs and recommend positions.
• Orchestrate execution across large, complex workload portfolios, aligning business and technical priorities across internal and external stakeholders to ensure long-term value realization.
• Architect scaling mechanisms, review cadences, and best practices that improve forecast accuracy, delivery fidelity, and operational efficiency across the customer’s organization and across AWS, not just within a single engagement.
• Influence product, engineering, and supply roadmaps based on patterns observed across strategic customers, and partner with engineering to build the tooling and simulation that improve demand forecasting, commitment tracking, and delivery visibility.
• Develop and mentor other team members, extending your influence and best practices across the capacity and customer solutions management community.


A day in the life
A typical day starts by checking in on the long-range initiatives you’re driving, whether that’s an upcoming executive briefing, a major GPU or ML buildout milestone, or a planning workshop with a customer’s infrastructure leaders. You might spend the morning with a customer’s VP of Infrastructure, walking through a multi-year scaling plan and pressure-testing forecast assumptions, then move into a room with EC2 Supply Chain and Finance leaders to present supportability scenarios for a significant capacity expansion and drive alignment on which to fund. Some days you are deep in a technical discussion on how a customer’s ML roadmap maps to Trainium and GPU supply; other days you are pulling together a business case, prepping a leadership review, or coaching a teammate through a complex customer situation. Given the size and complexity of these relationships, you will often be pulled into problems that have no obvious playbook, and that is part of what makes the role interesting.

Basic qualifications

- 10+ years of senior customer facing role experience
- 15+ years of leading complex, large-scale, IT, technical or engineering programs experience
- Bachelor's degree in Science, Technology, Engineering, Math, or a related field
- Experience in a senior customer-facing role
- Experience in leading complex, large-scale, IT, technical or engineering programs
- Experience working with current technologies (especially cloud)

Preferred qualifications

- PMP/SCRUM/Agile certification or are you SAFe certified
- Knowledge of key technology and market trends
- Knowledge of the software development/engineering lifecycle from conception to delivery
- Experience implementing AWS/cloud services

title: Senior Program Manager, SSD R2L Delivery, Central Operations Strategy
descriptionHtml:
The Central Operations Strategy organization is seeking a Sr. Program Manager to own weather and incident response strategy for our last-mile delivery network. Weather is one of the largest drivers of unplanned variability in our operations, and this role owns the mechanisms that determine how we respond to it: how much capacity we protect, how much volume we accept, and how quickly we recover when conditions differ from what was forecast.

This role sits at the intersection of operations strategy and data. The Sr. Program Manager will build and own the reporting and analysis that show how weather affects delivery performance, translate weather forecasts into clear capacity recommendations, and measure whether those recommendations improved outcomes. They will partner closely with our central response team, meteorologists, and business stakeholders to land the right balance between volume and delivery quality for every event, and to improve the quality of the inputs driving those decisions over time.

The role requires strong program ownership and comfort making decisions with imperfect information. The ideal candidate can dig into the data to find the answer, then turn it into a clear recommendation and a durable process that operations teams can run every day.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the framework that measures how weather affects delivery quality and capacity, and the recurring reporting built on it
- Build and maintain the models and analysis that turn weather forecasts into capacity and volume recommendations grounded in historical performance
- Measure forecast accuracy and recommendation effectiveness, and drive improvements from what you find
- Partner with our central response team to improve response playbooks, escalation paths, and recovery actions for planned and unplanned events
- Partner with meteorologists to improve forecasting, feeding operational outcomes back into how forecasts are built
- Own the volume-versus-quality trade-off recommendation, sizing the cost of both over-reacting and under-reacting
- Build the tools and processes that let this program scale across the network
- Influence investment priorities through data-driven business cases, and drive alignment across operations, planning, finance, and technology partners
- Communicate strategy, risks, and trade-offs to senior leadership
Demonstrated Competencies
- Strong analytical skills and the ability to work independently with large data sets; SQL and - Python preferred
- High judgment with incomplete information
- Track record of building programs or reporting capabilities from scratch
- Willingness to go deep in an unfamiliar, technically complex domain and become the expert others rely on
- Proven ability to build consensus and drive decisions across large, diverse stakeholder groups
- Ability to simplify complexity for senior audiences
- Confidence in ambiguous, fast-moving environments

A day in the life
You start by reviewing how the network performed against recent weather events, and where results missed, working backwards to whether the fix belongs in the forecast, the recommendation, or execution. You spend part of the day in the data, refining the analysis behind our capacity recommendations and quantifying trade-offs. You partner with the central response team to prepare for upcoming events and with meteorologists to review where forecasts diverged from outcomes. The rest of your time goes to building mechanisms rather than reacting: better reporting, less manual work, and the documents that take your recommendations to senior leadership.


Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment.

About the team
Central Operations Strategy owns the centralization strategy for order recovery, capacity management, and incident response across our last-mile delivery businesses. We centralize work that cannot scale at the site level, build automation to remove manual operational burden, and support the network through everything from new site launches to major disruptions. On the weather side, we measure how weather affects delivery performance, translate forecasts into capacity recommendations, and partner with meteorologists to improve forecast accuracy over time. We are a small team with broad ownership and the freedom to build what the network needs.

- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

- Experience using generative AI tools to accelerate program work — for example, building analysis and reporting prototypes, automating recurring manual tasks, or synthesizing large volumes of operational data into insights and written recommendations.

descriptionHtml:

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

title: Senior Power Electronics Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Are you excited about designing power-conversion hardware that will operate at megawatt scale inside data center infrastructure? Amazon Web Services is looking for a Senior Power Electronics Engineer to lead the design of solid-state transformer (SST) conversion stages, with deep expertise in high-voltage silicon carbide (SiC) devices and isolated high-power converter topologies.

You will own the dual active bridge (DAB), CLLC, and series-resonant converter stage designs from bench prototype through megawatt-class deployment, including SiC device selection and qualification. You will tackle device paralleling, current sharing, switching-loss optimization, and thermal derating challenges while guiding risk reduction through simulation and prototype correlation. You will also mentor fellow power electronics engineers, lead design reviews, and contribute to patent and technology decisions that shape the future of data center power delivery.



Key job responsibilities
- Lead architecture decisions for DAB, CLLC, and series-resonant converter stages, defining power-stage topologies that scale from prototype to megawatt deployment while meeting efficiency, thermal, and serviceability targets.
- Select and qualify high-voltage SiC power devices, evaluating switching losses, body-diode behavior, dynamic on-resistance, device paralleling, current sharing, and thermal derating for high-current operation.
- Coordinate converter-stage interfaces with the medium-voltage front end, 800 VDC output bus, controls, magnetics, and cooling subsystems to ensure cohesive system performance.
- Drive technical risk reduction through simulation, prototype testing, and measurement correlation, leading design reviews that set engineering quality standards across the team.
- Mentor power electronics engineers, contribute to patents and publications, and support technology roadmap decisions that advance data center power infrastructure.

A day in the life
You will split your time between hands-on design work and cross-functional collaboration. In a typical morning you might run converter simulations, review SiC device characterization data, or correlate prototype bench measurements against your models. Afternoons often shift to design reviews with magnetics, controls, and thermal engineers, or working sessions with partner teams on system-level interface specifications. You will regularly present technical trade-off analyses to stakeholders, coach junior engineers through design challenges, and carve out time to explore new converter architectures or draft patent disclosures.

About the team
Our team within AWS Infrastructure Services is focused on developing next-generation power delivery systems for data centers worldwide. We work at the intersection of power electronics, electrical infrastructure, and large-scale deployment, partnering closely with mechanical, controls, and construction engineering teams to bring new technology from concept to production.

We value an inclusive, collaborative culture where engineers at every level contribute ideas and learn from one another. If you are eager to solve complex power-conversion problems that directly improve the reliability and efficiency of global cloud infrastructure, this is the team for you.

descriptionHtml:

title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:

As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.


Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs
